- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., >0.4) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., <0.3) — model misses downward pressure, leading to lagged corrections.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in the short term after a spike, then underestimates the pullback.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/– values), model overreacts to recent sentiment shifts, causing erratic forecasts.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in the first 5–7 days after a spike, then converge — adjust early forecast peaks downward by 5–10% if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is rising (e.g., >0.6) and price is rising, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment is falling (e.g., <0.4) and price is falling, model often undercorrects — increase downward bias by 3–5% to align with sentiment.
